topic: Efficiency, BHP, IHP, FHP, SHP, knocking and detonation
syllabus_extract: Efficiency, BHP, IHP, FHP, SHP, knocking and detonation. Ignition system, basic principles, description and operations
specific_objectives: 22.1.1.1 Trainees will be able to explain about the working principle of piston engines.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of engine efficiency curves and ignition timing charts; Instructor supervision required for diagram interpretation.
intro_questions: What are the three main power outputs of a piston engine?
Define the term 'knocking' in the context of combustion.
Why is the ignition system critical for engine operation?

development.content:
Brake Horse Power definition
Indicated Horse Power calculation
Friction Horse Power relationship
Shaft Horse Power output
Engine efficiency types

Knocking causes and effects
Detonation vs normal combustion
Ignition system basic principles
Spark plug operation description
Ignition timing adjustments

Fuel octane rating impact
Cooling system role in detonation
Ignition system components overview
High tension lead function
Distributor operation basics

summary_questions: Explain the relationship between IHP, FHP, and BHP.
Describe the difference between knocking and detonation.
List three factors that influence ignition timing.
